newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares soar to fifth straight record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares soar to fifth straight record.

text.p: Shares on the Caracas Stock Exchange continued to resist profit-taking and soared to their fifth successive record close Thursday as foreign investors took medium- and long-term positions, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 2.31 percent to 5,177.04.
A total of 29 stocks closed higher, six lower and seven unchanged as investors bet on further booms for the market catalyzed by a series of forthcoming privatizations.

"Most stocks closed at record levels again due to continued interest from foreign investors who are motivated by the appearance of a good future for Venezuela's privatizations," said Hector Prez of the Financorp brokerage.
Prez added that it was clear that foreign investors were behind the market's rise because "they have not been taking profits. They invest thinking of the long and medium term."
Other brokers said the market was very active with foreign investors making an increasing presence.
"Many funds have recommended investing in Venezuela which is indicative of their confidence," said Gonzalo Alonso of the Activalores brokerage.

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 13.00 bolivars to 443.00 bolivars, steel company Sivensa rose 12.50 bolivars to 339.00 bolivars and agro- industrial company Mavesa rose 8.00 bolivars to 149.00 bolivars.
Trading was brisk with 4.575 billion bolivars ($9.7 million) changing hands.
Brokers said that after five successive rises, they expect profit-taking to set in at any moment, but stressed that the market's underlying trend remains bullish.
